speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, could you please describe when your symptoms first started and if they have worsened over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunken" walk and right-sided clumsiness suggest a coordination issue in the right cerebellum. To better localize the problem, do you notice any specific triggers for these symptoms, such as movement, or do you experience other issues like slurred speech or difficulty with fine motor tasks?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The combination of subacute cerebellar ataxia and a history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is highly suspicious for JC virus reactivation. I will proceed with MRI of the brain to confirm the presence of white matter lesions.
